docs.title: Chapter 1: Defining Your Research Question
docs.text:
Use the PICOT format to guide question design: - P: Population - I: Intervention - C: Comparison - O: Outcome - T: Timeframe

Example: "In adults with type 2 diabetes, does a plant-based diet compared to a low-carb diet improve HbA1c after 3 months?"

docs.title: Chapter 2: Understanding Variable Types
docs.text: Variable Type Scale Gender Categorical Nominal Pain Score Ordinal Ordinal HbA1c Continuous Ratio Temperature (C) Continuous Interval

docs.title: Chapter 3: Selecting the Right Statistical Test
docs.text:
Use this guide:

Objective Data Type Test Compare means (2 groups) Continuous, independent t-test Compare means (3+ groups) Continuous, multiple groups ANOVA Compare medians Ordinal or skewed Mann-Whitney U Compare proportions Categorical Chi-squared / Fisher Predict binary outcome Binary outcome, predictors Logistic regression

docs.title: Chapter 4: Hypothesis Testing and Inference
docs.text: Term Definition Null Hypothesis (H0) No difference Alternative (H1) There is a difference p-value Probability of observing this data if H0 were true Confidence Interval Range of likely values for an estimate Effect Size Magnitude of the observed effect

docs.title: Chapter 5: Comparing Two or More Groups
docs.text: Use: - t-test: two means - Paired t-test: same group before/after - Mann-Whitney U: two medians - ANOVA: more than 2 groups - Kruskal-Wallis: non-parametric alternative to ANOVA

docs.title: Chapter 6: Regression and Correlation
docs.text:
• Pearson correlation: linear relationship
  • Spearman: monotonic but not linear
  • Linear regression: continuous outcome
  • Logistic regression: binary outcome

docs.title: Chapter 7: Survival Analysis
docs.text: Used for time-to-event data: - Kaplan-Meier: plots survival probability - Log-rank test: compares curves - Cox regression: adjusts for covariates

docs.title: Chapter 8: Diagnostic Accuracy
docs.text: Key metrics: - Sensitivity: True positive rate - Specificity: True negative rate - PPV/NPV: Predictive values - ROC Curve: Discrimination ability

docs.title: Chapter 9: Ethics and Transparency
docs.text:
Avoid: - P-hacking - Selective reporting - Subgroup overuse without justification

Always: - Report effect sizes and confidence intervals - Pre-specify analysis plans

docs.title: Chapter 10: Practical Tips and Recap
docs.text:
• Match your test to your data type and design
  • Always check assumptions
  • Prefer confidence intervals and effect sizes
  • Consider clinical importance, not just p-values
